Here are our documents.

=== Notes ===
Sample (fictional)

Quillmere Rolling Library
Board meeting notes, October 21, 2026, Vashti Bend Community Room

Present: June Okafor-Reyes (board chair), Abner Whitlock (treasurer), Marisol Quennell (executive director), Pete Danforth (driver-librarian), Lila Ferrand (board member)

Item 3: Beaumont-Tully Rural Literacy Fund

Marisol reported that program officer Celeste Harrow at the Beaumont-Tully Rural Literacy Fund invited us to present Route Eighteen at their December 4 review. We will ask for $85,000 toward the $148,000 total. The county capital award of $40,000 is committed, and the spring donor campaign covers the last $23,000.

June asked for a short slide deck to go with the presentation. Marisol will own it. Draft to the board by November 20, 2026, final to Celeste by November 27.

1. Keep it to eight slides or fewer. Ms. Harrow said reviewers get ten minutes per applicant.
2. Open with the problem: 11 missed stops last year, all from the 2009 vehicle, and four north-county schools with 310 students waiting to join.

response.draft:
Slide 1: Route Eighteen: Stops We Missed and Schools Still Waiting
Quillmere Rolling Library, Vashti Bend, Corrow County
FY2026: we missed 11 of 292 scheduled stops
All 11 were caused by one vehicle: our 2009 bookmobile, now past 214,000 miles
Each missed school stop means a class waits four weeks between visits, not two
Four north-county schools are waiting to join: Dunmore, Pike Hollow, Sayer Flat, East Kettle
310 K-6 students, and none of the four schools has a school librarian
We cannot add them with one aging vehicle that already misses stops

Slide 2: Who We Serve
A two-person bookmobile for rural elementary schools with no school librarian
Every school we serve is more than 25 miles from the nearest public library branch
2025-26: 14 schools, 1,180 K-6 students
A visit every other week for 36 weeks, plus 40 summer stops at churches, a feed store lot and the county fairgrounds
Sixth year of service

Slide 3: FY2026 Results
Stops completed: 281 of 292 (96 percent)
Items checked out: 21,460, up from 18,930 in FY2025
Return rate: 91 percent
New county library cards issued to students: 846
Summer reading: 214 children enrolled, 131 finished the eight-book goal
Classroom crate loans, new this year: 52 of 61 teachers took part, about 4,100 checkouts

Slide 4: The Vehicle Is Wearing Out
October: lost a transmission line
February: failed its brake inspection
June: overheated twice
Vehicle costs rose from $19,700 to $31,900 in one year, almost all of it repairs
"Bookmobile Tuesday is the only day the whole class runs to the window. When you missed in February, three kids asked me if you were coming back." (Dorrie Akin, third-grade teacher, Fallow Creek Elementary)

Slide 5: The Plan: Route Eighteen
Buy a smaller second vehicle: a used high-roof cargo van with shelving and a wheelchair lift
The van runs a new north route that adds the four waiting schools
The 2009 bookmobile stays on the shorter southern route through FY2028 while we save for its replacement
With two vehicles, a breakdown on one route no longer cancels every stop
Full service: 18 schools, about 1,490 students, 324 school stops a year

Slide 6: The Full Cost: $148,000
Used high-roof cargo van: $74,000
Refit (shelving, wheelchair lift, inverter, mobile hotspot): $18,500
Opening collection for four new schools (2,400 books): $21,600
Added driver-librarian hours, 0.5 FTE, year one: $26,400
Driver training, vehicle signage, launch visits: $3,500
Contingency: $4,000
Total: $148,000 (one-time costs plus first-year added operating cost)

Slide 7: Three Funding Sources
Corrow County Library District one-time capital award: $40,000 (committed)
Beaumont-Tully Rural Literacy Fund: $85,000 (this request)
Spring 2027 donor campaign: $23,000 (planned)
Total: $148,000
Our operating base is steady: the county contract and the Voss Family Foundation grant are renewed for FY2027, and the state grant runs through June 2027

Slide 8: What We Know About Reading, and the Timeline
Six of our 14 schools shared spring third-grade benchmark results (188 students)
At those six schools, third graders at or above grade level went from 41 percent (spring 2025) to 49 percent (spring 2026)
The state placed part-time reading tutors in four of those six schools that same year
We cannot separate our effect from the tutors' effect, and we do not claim this gain
Other limits: there is no comparison group, and the schools that volunteered their data may not be typical
Next year: benchmark data from all 14 schools and checkouts tracked per student
Timeline if fully funded by March 2027: van bought and refitted in spring, north-route summer stops in June 2027, full school service in August 2027
FY2027 goals: miss no more than three stops, get data from all 14 current schools, have the van on the north route by June 2027
